title: Vehicle Emergency Kit
description: Use this list to stock every car for breakdowns, crashes, and being stranded in any season.

sources.title: Anatomy of a First Aid Kit

items.text: First aid kit in a hard, sealed case with gloves, bleeding control, trauma shears, and an emergency blanket per seat
Jumper cables or a charged jump starter
Reflective warning triangles or road flares, and a reflective vest
Spare tire checked for air, jack, and lug wrench - or a tire inflator and sealant kit if you have no spare
Water: at least 1 gallon (3.8 L), rotated every 6 months
Car phone charger and a charged power bank
Flashlight or headlamp with spare lithium batteries
Keep the fuel tank at least half full so you can evacuate or run the heater if stranded
Non-perishable snacks such as energy bars and nuts
Blanket for each regular passenger
Paper road map of your region
Basic tool kit: multi-tool, screwdrivers, pliers, duct tape, zip ties
Seatbelt cutter and window breaker tool mounted within the driver's reach
Small fire extinguisher rated for vehicles, strapped down
Work gloves and a rain poncho
Comfortable walking shoes and a warm layer
Cat litter or sand for traction, and an ice scraper in cold months
Written emergency contacts, insurance card, and roadside assistance number
Tow strap and a quart of motor oil and coolant
Whistle and a bright cloth to signal for help
Strap down heavy items so they do not fly forward in a crash; keep the first aid kit reachable if the trunk is jammed
Check the kit every spring and fall - heat ruins medicines, food, and batteries in parked cars
